lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- Holding the Floor: Opinion, Agreement and Polite Disagreement
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Dejair Caitano do Nascimento | Lesson 7 -- Holding the Floor

listenings.text: Before we open the discussion, one word about how it works in this room. When you disagree with somebody here, you are not attacking them. You are doing your job. But there is a way to do it that keeps the conversation alive, and a way that ends it. The way that ends it is to say the person is wrong. The way that keeps it alive is to point at the evidence, not at the person. Say what you agree with first, then say what you would challenge, and then give your reason. Three steps, always in that order. And if you are not sure of your English, say less, not more. A short sentence with a clear reason is stronger than three long ones.

I want to raise one point about the conclusion, and I say this with respect, because I like this study very much. The authors conclude that the treatment does not work in older patients. I agree with the data. I do not agree with the conclusion. Look at how they selected the group. All the older patients came from one hospital, and that hospital only sees the most severe cases. So the result may be about severity, not about age. I would rather say the treatment works less well in severe cases, and leave age out of it until we have better evidence. That is my point, and I am happy to be wrong.
